items.body: Blog post: https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/llama-cpp-v1 ## Overview llama.cpp v1.0.0 removes the deprecated public API and promotes the NextN/speculative API to `llama.h`, adds OCP FP8 KV caches, a host-memory MoE expert cache with a configurable CPU share, and loading of external PLE shards. It adds three text architectures (Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Ripple and xing4_0), drama-3 TTS, and MageVL-Cowork and Kimi-K3.1 vision, hardens `llama-server` (SSRF, CORS, DNS rebinding, MCP tool cancellation) and adds a `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint, ships a redesigned web UI with chat groups and a markdown editor, and updates `ggml` to v1.0.0. ### API changes - llama.h: remove `llama_set_warmup`, 35 deprecated functions, `defrag_thold` and `--defrag-thold` ([#30565](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30565)) - llama.h: promote the NextN API from `llama-ext.h` and rename `llama_set_embd_state_src` to `llama_set_ctx_state_src` ([#30565](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30565)) - llama.h: add `moe_cache_size` and `moe_cache_cpu_share` to `llama_context_params` ([#30966](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30966)) - mtmd.h: add `MTMD_GEN_AUDIO_TYPE_DRAMA3` and `temp` in `mtmd_helper_gen_audio_inp` ([#31613](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31613), [#31655](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31655)) - mtmd-helper.h: add `mtmd_helper_resampler` for streaming raw PCM at the model sample rate ([#31964](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31964)) - server: add the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint and a `temperature` option for `/tts` ([#31763](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31763), [

items.name: b12360
items.body:
<details open>

CUDA: split the PAD_REFLECT_1D grid to stay within the HIP grid limit (#32179)

The kernel launches one block per row and 256-wide tile, so the
{2, 16777217} test case asks for 16777217 blocks of 256 threads. HIP
refuses a grid dimension above 2^32 threads and the ROCm jobs fail
with "invalid configuration argument".

The host now launches the grid in chunks of at most UINT32_MAX / 256
blocks and passes the chunk offset to the kernel. Real sizes fit in a
single chunk and keep their timings.

</details>

items.name: Release v5.23.0
items.body: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50682) ### JEV JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`. **Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental.
